MINUTES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MARCH 25, 2024

 1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
 A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
 called to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall

 Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas announced that as noted in a memo that went
 out to the Equestrian Committee members the previous week, the City would be
 contracting out preparation of the Committee’s meeting minutes.

 2.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Griggs, Martin, Nilsen, Shinn, Pope,
  Romanelli and Schachter
  Committee Members Absent:  Harik and Silvano
  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

 3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
 A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 22, 2024

  CHAIR SCHACHTER noted a correction made to the proposed Draft Minutes of
  January 22, 2024 to Supervisor Pinuelas.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated the correction to be made as follows: Section H, in the
  first paragraph under the Equestrian Issues Log, adding the word “not” to the
  sentence so it reads, “Chair Schachter thanked Superintendent Goldsmith and his
  staff for their work and noted that the issues are not only equestrian related”.

  MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER GRIGGS to:

  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY 22, 2024, EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS CORRECTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

 4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  NONE.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 25, 2024
  5.  BUSINESS ITEMS
 A.  INTRODUCTION OF NEW COMMITTEE MEMBERS (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR SCHACHTER welcomed new Committee Members Lisa Van Pope and Jeff
  Romanelli who are the representatives from the Parks and Activities Commission
  and the Planning Commission, respectively.

 B.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS LIST

  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that Supervisor Pinuelas would present the staff
  report, and added that there would be a Policy Development meeting on March 26,
  2024, with the City Council and staff where they would be addressing any Capital
  Improvement Projects (CIP) including those from the Equestrian Committee.

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.

  MEMBER SHINN inquired if the mural at Ernie Howlett Park could be updated.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that the mural had been repainted prior to the COVID-
  19 pandemic.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the date the mural was repainted was listed
  on the side of the wall.

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis stated that it could be added to a future project
  list to be repainted, especially if wear and tear becomes apparent.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired if the equestrian structures at Ernie Howlett Park
  were in need of paint.

  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that paint was not needed, but the facia
  boards on the entry booth and dressage building need to be replaced, and would
  be addressed by maintenance staff.

  MEMBER SHINN inquired if the pickleball activities at Ernie Howlett Park were loud.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that no complaints regarding pickleball activity noise
  levels had been received.

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that when looking towards the barn and the bathroom,
  the roofs appear to slope towards each other and asked if the barn was structurally
  sound.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 25, 2024
   Superintendent Goldsmith confirmed that the barn is structurally sound and noted
  that a drain is located in between the barn and bathroom structures.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if there were thoughts regarding prioritization of the
  CIP List and noted that driving through the parking lot was an issue after a rainfall.

  ACM Davis explained the process regarding the budget, CIP list and prioritization
  for the current and future year(s).

  MEMBER POPE inquired about the assessment of the sand volleyball and
  basketball court areas at Ernie Howlett Park and whether another use would be
  considered for the space.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that staff was reviewing how the space could be better
  utilized now that sand volleyball area was not frequently used. She noted that since
  the basketball courts are used frequently, staff was assessing whether to keep them
  in their current location, relocate them, or convert to half courts to open up space
  since most people use only one basket at a time.

  MEMBER POPE noted the item related to potential space for a dog park or dog run
  and stated that the Parks and Activities Commission would work in partnership with
  the Equestrian Committee on the item. She stated that based on reports of dogs off
  leash in the parks, that there was clearly a need for a dog park or dog run.

  MEMBER NILSEN commented regarding owners of dogs who run off leash in parks
  possibly not wanting their dogs to socialize with other dogs versus owners of dogs
  who like to socialize with other dogs and would frequent a potential dog park.

  ACM Davis noted that the Dog Park Feasibility Study was being presented to City
  Council on March 26, 2024, to see if it is a priority and if staff should continue to
  research the potential dog park.

  MEMBER SHINN expressed her concern regarding the location of a potential dog
  park in reference to it being a disadvantage to the horses and a safety issue.

  MEMBER ROMANELLI commented that he viewed the painting of Ernie Howlett
  Park equestrian structures as maintenance projects, as they are existing structures
  that need to be maintained.

  C. MAY MEETING DATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Equestrian Committee’s next regular meeting
  date in May falls on Memorial Day and recommended the Committee discuss an

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 25, 2024
   alternative meeting date for May 2024. She suggested that the Committee may
  want to consider Monday, May 20, 2024, which is the third Monday of the month
  and noted there were no other meetings scheduled that day.

  As the Committee had no objections to Monday, May 20, 2024 for the next meeting,
  the Monday, May 27, 2024 meeting would be canceled and the next meeting would
  be on Monday, May 20, 2024, at 7:00 p.m.

 6.  STAFF ITEMS

 A.  2024 HORSE TRAINER LICENSE AND PERMIT UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update regarding the 2024 Licensed Horse
  Trainer List. She reported that those listed as pending were in the process of having
  their licenses and permits updated.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired about Thole Farms (Ludger Thole) being listed as
  Category 1 and about Maverick Farms (Linda Cooper). CHAIR SCHACHTER also
  noted other trainers not currently on the list and encouraged staff to reach out to
  them.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that staff is currently looking to confirm if Thole Farms
  is in the appropriate category and clarified that all trainers that are not listed have
  to apply and pay for a city business license for a permit, or there is another
  requirement they have not yet met, such as submittal of an insurance certificate
  and hold harmless statement. She confirmed that the Finance Department would
  be working with trainers during this process.

 B.  TRANSPORTATION ENHANCEMENT AND AMERICANS WITH DISABILITY ACT
  IMPROVEMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND
  LONDON LANE (DAPPLEGRAY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL)

  ACM Davis provided a verbal overview per written report. She reported that the
  Project will be presented again to City Council at the second meeting in April 2024
  to review and give staff guidance. She stated that this project was originally
  presented to City Council in the Fall of 2023, and staff was directed to do additional
  outreach to help the community better understand the plan. She reviewed the plan
  details including enhancing traffic and pedestrian signals, the improvement of traffic
  flow, ADA access, pedestrian and equestrian safety, and the funding sources. She
  stated that this report was brought to the Equestrian Committee to explain the
  impacts for equestrians and those who use the trails, which are expected to be
  minimal. She noted that Phase One of the project would not begin until Summer of
  2025 and Phase Two would begin Summer of 2026.

  MEMBER NILSEN inquired about what would be added regarding traffic calming
  for this project.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 25, 2024
   ACM Davis stated that Willdan Engineering is the engineering firm for this project
  and provided a general overview in response to MEMBER NILSEN.

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that she had attended the City Council meeting when
  the proposed project was first presented and that she sees many modifications
  which addressed the concerns expressed.

  MEMBER SHINN stated that she also attended the City Council meeting when the
  proposed project was first presented and stated that there was a lot of money being
  spent when staggered school hours may be more effective.

  MEMBER BRTIS inquired about the proposed project potentially adding more street
  for equestrians to cross between trails, because the crosswalk did not seem
  aligned.

  ACM Davis noted that she did not believe that there would be any impact to the
  horse trails, but that she would confirm with the Public Works Director.

  MEMBER MARTIN clarified that the trail was already offset from the crosswalk.

  MEMBER ROMANELLI confirmed that this proposed project had been coordinated
  with the Traffic and Safety Committee. He inquired if any consideration had been
  made for a very similar problem at Rancho Vista Elementary School at Palos
  Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Lane. He requested that it be considered as
  part of the long-term plan for transportation enhancement and traffic and safety.
  ACM DAVIS said she would report that comment to the Public Works Department
  for further research.

 C.  EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE (VERBAL
  REPORT)

  ACM Davis reported that the Emergency Preparedness Subcommittee reconvened
  that day, and shared the following: the website would be updated, the RHE horse
  text alert is utilized, micro-chip training and equine safety training will be held again
  in the future, zones were identified in the city and water caches have been placed,
  they have been working with the Palos Verdes Peninsula Horseman’s Association
  to have a Facebook page to record trail conditions, and will develop an RHE
  Emergency Preparedness book to share with the community. She clarified that
  there were emergency halters in City vehicles and will work with the Sheriff to
  ensure they also have them. She gave an update on the Polaris (4-wheel ATV
  vehicle) that the Sheriff’s Department had recommissioned, maintained, and would
  receive training on soon to monitor hot spots, safety, and emergency aspects while
  being cognizant of equestrian safety.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 25, 2024
  D.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOM PROJECT UPDATE
  (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis reported on the status of the modular restroom facility to be placed and
  connected to existing plumbing at the Peter Weber Equestrian Center. She stated
  that staff hoped it would be installed within the next few months. She noted that
  there have been challenges with the Los Angeles County Health Department due
  to the restroom’s proximity to the landfill, so staff has been communicating with the
  Sanitation District, County land/leasing office, Public Health Department, and the
  County Supervisor to resolve the issue. She added that the City was now paying
  for the existing Port-a-Potties at the site.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER requested verification that the Port-a-Potties be serviced
  twice per week, especially due to the increased use with birthday party reservations.
  Superintendent Goldsmith affirmed and noted that they have been replaced with
  brand new units and that another handicapped unit had been added.

  MEMBER GRIGGS inquired if the modular unit could be placed at the site now but
  raised so it could be considered as a Port-a-Potty unit. ACM Davis responded that
  the modular unit was too heavy to be placed in a raised position.

 E.  SHARING TRAILS SAFETY OUTREACH VIDEO (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that the videos were filmed earlier this month and
  were being edited. She thanked Member Shinn and Council Member Schachter for
  their assistance and guidance. She stated that the videos should be done in mid-
  April, and that they would be posted online, and on the City’s social media channels.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the videos would be 30 seconds to one minute long
  with a voiceover and would be released one at a time on social media in response
  to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  MEMBER SHINN suggested that another video be made showing a horse being
  approached by vehicles being driven on the trail.

 F.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that this year’s event was scheduled for Saturday,
  May 11, 2024, from 8:30 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. She stated that the invitations had been
  sent out and requested that the committee members let her know if they would be
  attending. She noted that the Scouts were on board to host the traditional Pancake
  Breakfast.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 25, 2024
  G.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  MEMBER SHINN inquired about a mounting block to be placed outside Chandler
  Arena and whether the Scouts could assist.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER noted that there was a mounting block inside the Chandler
  Arena.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the Scouts have not reached out to him yet
  to assist, but that he was waiting to hear back from a scout who expressed interest
  in helping.

  MEMBER SHINN asked about the uneven trail on PVDN crossing over driveway.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the trail had been scraped, but repairs have
  not yet been completed as there was another rain event expected over the
  weekend.

  MEMBER POPE inquired about the reporting mechanism for the Equestrian Issues
  Log. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he receives reports via phone calls and
  text messages on an ongoing basis, as well as from people who come into City
  Hall, and issues that staff members find and report.

  Superintendent Goldsmith confirmed that he maintains the Equestrian Issues Log
  database, in response to MEMBER ROMANELLI.

  MEMBER BRTIS inquired about a cement structure on the road near the Rolling
  Hills Little League baseball fields at Dapplegray Elementary School which drops
  water down the canyon. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the water was
  coming from an adjacent city. He confirmed that the School District-owned road had
  been backfilled by the District where part of the road had been lost, and that it was
  sheeted off but they have not altered the flow of the water.

  Discussion continued regarding water on the trail. Superintendent Goldsmith stated
  that Strawberry Lane had not cleaned out their culverts, so water was flowing
  across the horse trails. He also stated the private arena at Dapplegray was affected
  and stated there was not much that could be done until the rain slowed down.

  MEMBER BRTIS noted that the school must have closed off that road because
  people were driving on the horse trails.

  MEMBER NILSEN confirmed that the road at Dapplegray Elementary School was
  open again.

 H.  MATTERS OF INTEREST

  NONE.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 25, 2024
  7.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

 A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that there have been five land erosion that have
  restricted the width of the riding trails, and inquired when the trails would be
  smoothed out. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that staff was waiting for the
  trails to dry out so they could repair them safely and noted that it is on the schedule.

 B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

 8.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

 A.  TRAIL SAFETY FOR SHERIFF PATROL

  ACM Davis stated that a Sheriff representative would attend a meeting so the
  Committee could provide them with input regarding trail safety, in response to
  MEMBER SHINN.

 9.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHACHTER ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:03 pm.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Pam Brown Schachter
  Community Services Supervisor  Chair

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 25, 2024
